capture.final_message:
Treat the conjunction’s two equivalences extensionally: prove all four universally quantified statements independently, then assemble each equivalence because both sides are true.

The common mechanism is the pointwise refinement characterization of a topological basis.

- Basis enlargement: every member of \(s'\) is open, and any open neighborhood is refined by some member of \(s\), hence by a member of \(s'\) using \(s\subseteq s'\).

- Product projection: use the standard finite-cylinder basis of the product topology. The image under evaluation at \(i\) of a nonempty basic cylinder is either its \(i\)-th open factor or the whole space, so evaluation is an open map.

- Quotient basis: images of members of \(V\) are open by the assumed openness of the quotient map. Given an open neighborhood downstairs, lift a point to \(X\), refine its open preimage by a member of \(V\), and map that member back down.

- Product basis: finite intersections of inverse images under coordinate projections form the usual product basis. Refine each of the finitely many coordinate-open sets by an element of \(T_i\); the resulting set is exactly a finite-support box `Set.pi ↑F U`.

The openness assumption on the quotient map is the essential extra hypothesis: without it, images of basis elements need not be open.
